item.title: Present continuous: what is happening now
item.explanation_text: Use am, is or are + verb-ing for actions that are happening now, at the moment you speak: I am reading. She is cooking. They are playing football. Negatives: I'm not working. He isn't sleeping. They aren't listening. Questions: Are you listening? Is it raining? Spelling: most verbs add -ing (read → reading). If the verb ends in -e, drop the -e (make → making). Short verbs like sit, run and swim double the last letter (sitting, running, swimming).
item.contrast_text: Compare: I drink tea every morning (a habit, present simple). I am drinking tea now (at this moment, present continuous).
item.common_error_pattern: Leaving out am, is or are ('She cooking'), or forgetting -ing after am, is or are ('I am read').

examples.bad: They are play football in the park.
examples.good: They are playing football in the park.

examples.bad: I am siting on the bus.
examples.good: I am sitting on the bus.
